messages:
Alice Nguyen: FYI — EU-WEST dedicated slice started mass preemptions at 09:14 UTC, latency for small chat workloads jumped ~210ms.
Ben Ortiz: Can you drop the scheduler traces? Any pattern (PCIe, nvlink, egress) :thinking: 
Alice Nguyen: quick log dump:
```
allocator: slice=dedicated-eu-west-3 id=sd-42 util=95% spikes=pcie_retries
evict: tenants=preemptible-3,4,8 reason=noisy_neighbor
net: egress_q=high for tenant=mlprep-batch
```
Carla Mendes: @Alice thanks. Two things: 1) run the handoff sequencer to drain noisy tenants with `handoff mode=staggered` 2) route latency-sensitive tokens to reserved-dedicated pools in eu-west-2 for the short term.
Dave Liu: cost calc: routing 15% of traffic cross-region adds ~$4.2k/day for bandwidth + 5% compute premium. Is that acceptable?
Alice Nguyen: prefer targeted canary — only move QoS=low batch tenants and models with token cost<50k/day. That keeps egress small.
Ben Ortiz: started sequencer run: `seqctl start --slice sd-42 --mode staggered --limit 10` — infra-bot will post progress.
infra-bot: seqctl: started handoff for sd-42 at 09:28 UTC. draining 10 tenants/hr. progress=0/14
Carla Mendes: also proposing a short-term routing tweak: in routing-policies add `prefer: dedicated && latency_sensitive=false -> eu-west-2` expire in 1h.
Dave Liu: ack, set budget alert at $5k/day for cross-region shift.
Alice Nguyen: monitoring pcie error counters & KV cache miss rates; will report in 30m.
Ben Ortiz: if this repeats let's consider temporary hard-isolation for sd-42 and offer affected customers a discount.
Alice Nguyen: thanks team :thumbsup:
